summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ 3.13.7 cluster (node1/node2/node3, RHEL9) with AMQP-over-TLS as the only client listener, mandatory client-certificate authentication against a cluster-dedicated CA, and a management interface bound to each node's private IP and firewall-restricted to the cluster subnet. Each node was then sequentially rebooted via the mandatory restart protocol, with boot-id changes and full cluster/TLS/management recovery proven on every node.
actions_performed: Installed Erlang 26.2.5.4 and RabbitMQ 3.13.7 on node1, node2, node3 via the official RabbitMQ packagecloud RPM repos
Generated a dedicated CA on node1 (openssl, 4096-bit key, 10y validity) plus per-node server certs (SAN=hostname+IP) and one client certificate, all signed by that CA
Distributed CA cert and per-node server cert/key to /etc/rabbitmq/tls on each node via scp over the cluster SSH key, with rabbitmq:rabbitmq ownership and 640/644 perms
Generated a fresh shared Erlang cookie on node1 and distributed it securely to node2/node3 for clustering

Configured rabbitmq.conf on all nodes: listeners.tcp = none (TLS-only AMQP on 5671), ssl_options.verify=verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, management.tcp.ip bound to each node's private IP only, classic_config peer discovery listing all 3 nodes
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin and started rabbitmq-server on all nodes
Opened firewalld rich rules restricting ports 4369/25672/5671/15672 to the 10.100.157.0/24 cluster subnet only (initial join_cluster failed with noconnection until this was added)
Joined node2 and node3 to node1's cluster via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; verified 3/3 running nodes with no partitions
Verified TLS enforcement: openssl s_client without a client cert receives fatal alert 'certificate_required'; with the CA-issued client cert, handshake succeeds (verify return code 0)
Created appuser and ran a Python/pika end-to-end publish+consume test over AMQPS using the client certificate
Confirmed no plaintext 5672 listener exists anywhere; 15672 bound only to each node's private IP, not 0.0.0.0
Confirmed management API reachable cross-node within the cluster subnet (node2 -> node1:15672)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on each node, then restarted node1, node2, node3 one at a time using systemctl reboot, polling until each came back with a new boot_id
After each restart, verified rabbitmq-server active, full 3/3 cluster quorum restored, and (for node1) re-ran the TLS cert-required check and pubsub test to confirm functional recovery

evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3 all listed as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with no partitions, after join_cluster succeeded on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: AMQP served only over TLS (no plaintext listener)
evidence.summary: ss -tlnp on all three nodes shows no port 5672 listener; port 5671 (AMQPS) is listening on all interfaces

evidence.requirement: Cluster-created CA and only CA-issued client certs accepted
evidence.summary: CA and per-node/client certs generated locally on node1; TLS handshake to 5671 without a client cert yields fatal alert 'certificate_required'; handshake with the CA-issued client cert succeeds (verify return code 0)

evidence.requirement: Functional AMQPS client access using CA-issued cert
evidence.summary: Python/pika client using the CA-issued client cert connected over amqps, published and consumed a message ('hello-over-tls') successfully

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only within the cluster
evidence.summary: management.tcp.ip bound to each node's own private IP (not 0.0.0.0); firewalld rich rules restrict ports 4369/25672/5671/15672 to the 10.100.157.0/24 cluster subnet; cross-node curl from node2 to node1:15672 reached the HTTP API (proving in-cluster reachability)

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 98aa35f5... and healthcheck ok captured; systemctl reboot issued; node unreachable then returned with new boot_id 882a1131...; cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running again; TLS cert-required and management healthcheck re-verified

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery, quorum preserved
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f1afbc7f... (captured earlier); reboot issued; node unreachable then returned with new boot_id dac6802e...; cluster_status and rabbitmq-diagnostics check_running confirm full 3-node quorum restored

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery, quorum preserved
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b634b53f... (captured earlier); reboot issued; node unreachable then returned with new boot_id 87add4ba...; cluster_status and rabbitmq-diagnostics check_running confirm full 3-node quorum restored

evidence.requirement: Final post-restart end-to-end verification of the entire task
evidence.summary: After all 3 sequential restarts: cluster_status shows 3/3 running nodes, a fresh TLS pubsub test with the client cert succeeded, and the management healthcheck returned ok
